blocks.x: New York’s fall foliage season still has plenty of good weekends up its sleeve, and one of our favorite Hudson Valley escapes could be saving its brightest colors for Halloween!

Beacon, the riverside city known for its art-filled former Nabisco factory and shop-lined Main Street, is forecast to reach peak foliage from October 27 through November 2, according to the Explore Fall forecast.
That puts Halloween weekend right in the middle of its predicted window.
And with a direct train from Grand Central taking about 90 minutes, you don’t even need to rent a car or spend half your Saturday getting there.

Once you arrive, you can make the day as ambitious or as leisurely as you like: climb above the Hudson for sweeping mountain views, browse your way along Main Street, or settle in for lunch overlooking a waterfall. There’s also a nearly 300,000-square-foot art museum waiting when you’re ready to head indoors.
It’s maybe one of this year’s best Halloween plans — and we have all the details on how to plan the fall escape.

When will Beacon’s fall foliage peak?
Explore Fall’s Beacon forecast puts the expected peak window at October 27 to November 2, making Saturday, October 31, and Sunday, November 1, especially tempting dates for a visit.
Of course, the leaves aren’t working from a shared calendar.
Color can arrive at different times along the riverfront and up on Mount Beacon, where the elevation can shift the timing even within the same outing.
Explore Fall cautions that its maps are only mere estimates, with local terrain and forest composition affecting when a destination reaches its best color (but they’re pretty accurate!).
Think of these dates as your planning window, then check the forecast and the I LOVE NY weekly foliage report again before hopping on the train.
Why Beacon is worth watching later this month
While some New Yorkers are already heading north for peak foliage, Beacon’s forecast gives you something to look forward to closer to Halloween.

This week’s reports describe parts of the Adirondacks as already moving past peak, with several Catskills destinations much farther along in their color change. The Hudson Valley’s historical peak season stretches later, from mid-October into early November, so missing an early-October mountain getaway doesn’t mean you’ve missed your chance.
And Beacon has an advantage beyond its timing: there’s enough here to fill a day even when you’re not staring at the trees.
Start with mountain views or a walk beside the Hudson
For the big panoramic payoff, head to Mount Beacon Park.

The fall trail follows the route of the city’s old incline railway, beginning with stairs before climbing through steep switchbacks. At the overlook, the Hudson Highlands and river open up below you, with views stretching toward the Catskills.

It’s a proper uphill hike, so bring suitable shoes and leave enough time to get back down before dark. You can continue toward the South Mount Beacon fire tower for a longer outing, but the first overlook already gives you plenty to stop and admire.

For a gentler start, Long Dock Park trades the climb for a riverfront wander. Its 19 acres include restored wetlands, meadows, and picnic spots, making it an easy place to slow down before heading into town.

Photo: Shutterstock
Leave plenty of time for Main Street and a waterfall-side lunch
The best part of a Beacon day trip might be that you don’t need to plan every minute.

Main Street stretches for over a mile, with independent bookshops, galleries, boutiques, antique stores, cafés, and restaurants giving you plenty of reasons to keep stopping. Come for a walk, spot a shop you like, and let the afternoon take it from there.

For a sit-down meal, The Roundhouse pairs seasonal, locally sourced food with views of Fishkill Creek and the falls. Its floor-to-ceiling windows make the waterfall part of lunch, rather than another stop to squeeze into your itinerary.

Visiting on Sunday, November 1? The Beacon Farmers’ Market runs from 10 am to 2 pm, year-round and rain or shine. You can work a market browse into your downtown wander before heading back toward the river.
Step inside Beacon’s enormous former Nabisco factory
A fall trip to Beacon doesn’t have to be entirely outdoors.

Dia Beacon occupies a former Nabisco box-printing factory built in 1929, now filled with art from the 1960s onward. The nearly 300,000-square-foot building is a destination in its own right, and it’s only an eight-to-ten-minute walk from the station.
It’s a particularly good addition to a riverfront-and-Main-Street day, or an alternative when the weather isn’t cooperating.

Just give yourself time to enjoy it. Dia suggests allowing two to three hours for a visit, so pairing the museum with a full mountain hike could leave your supposedly relaxing escape feeling a little rushed. Current published hours are Friday through Monday, 10 am to 5 pm, though you should check seasonal hours and admission details before visiting!
How to get to Beacon from NYC

Take Metro-North’s Hudson Line from Grand Central directly to Beacon. The journey takes about 90 minutes, depending on the train, and you can check departure times through the MTA’s current schedules.
From there, build your day around the part of Beacon you’re most excited to explore: a riverfront wander, an afternoon browsing Main Street, or a hike up Mount Beacon.
For an easy first visit, stick with the riverfront and downtown, leaving time for a museum stop or lunch beside the falls.
Going for the mountain views? Catch an earlier train and save Main Street for after the hike.
Either way, Beacon’s forecast gives you a good excuse to keep one more fall weekend free.
The post This popular riverside Hudson Valley city near NYC is forecast to hit peak fall foliage over Halloween weekend appeared first on Secret NYC.
